name: AWP American Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's top title, meant for its hardest worker and defended at least once a month. "Elite Sensation" Eric Emerson held it in June 2001; Sinister won it by making Andy Madison submit in a cage match, and retained it against his own partner, the Professional, on Breakdown in December 2001.

name: AWP Can-Am Championship
epitaph: A title whose holder stands first in line for a heavyweight title match. Steve Jensen held it in June 2001 and kept it against the Professional on Total Darkness, before the title was merged into the Triple Crown.

name: AWP Television Championship
epitaph: The title for the best of the federation's television wrestling, defended more often than any other. Hiroyoshi Takada held it in June 2001; Vincenzo Sandora came away with it from Ready to Rumble II, though Chris Johnson, the last man standing in that night's battle royal, claimed it was his.

name: AWP Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Added in late 2001 to spotlight the federation's cruiserweight division. Ben Tuckwell held it in November 2001 and lost it to Ashlyn Summers on RAGE in December, when the special referee, Brian Taylor, turned on him.

name: AWP Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The title for the federation's best two-man team. The PPD, Lance and Max Studd, won it for a second time from the American Renegades and held it in June 2001; after it fell vacant, the Conceptuals were champions by late November 2001 and retained against the Down South Connection on RAGE in December.

name: AWP Fight Club Championship
epitaph: The title for the federation's street fighters. BIG GUY won it at Spring Riot with the PPD's help and was billed to put it up in an open challenge in June 2001, before the title was merged into the Triple Crown.

name: AWP Triple Crown Championship
epitaph: Created from a merger of the Fight Club, Can-Am and New Age titles. Steve Jensen held it by November 2001 and retained it against the Motor City Madman on RAGE in December.
